title: Ornithology
tagline: The study of birds, from museums to field guides.
source: Generated from “Timeline of ornithology” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Avicenna
events.text: Death of Abu ‘Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina (known as Avicenna in Latin) author of Abbreviatio de animalibus, a homage to Aristotle

events.title: Clusius
events.text: Clusius publishes Exoticorum libri decem ("Ten books of exotics") in which he describes many new exotic species.

events.title: Aristotle
events.text: 4th century BC – Aristotle mentions over 170 sorts of birds in his work on animals. He recognises eight principal groups.

events.title: Georg Steller
events.text: Georg Steller studies the birds of the north Pacific on his voyage with Vitus Bering

events.title: Philibert Commerçon
events.text: 1769 French naturalist Philibert Commerçon accompanies Louis Antoine de Bougainville on a voyage of circumnavigation

events.title: Juan Ignacio Molina
events.text: Juan Ignacio Molina publishes Saggio sulla storia naturale del Chile which includes the first descriptions of many South American species

events.title: Blasius Merrem
events.text: “de Arte Venandi cum Avibus” by Frederick II (d. 1250) published and compared favorably to contemporary science by Blasius Merrem and Johan Gottlobb Schneider

events.title: Pacific Ocean
events.text: "Le Geographe" and "Le Naturaliste" leave France for the Pacific Ocean under the overall command of Nicolas Baudin. The naturalists on board made a collection of over 100,000 zoological specimens. Many bird species will be described by Louis Pierre V

events.title: Peter Simon Pallas
events.text: Publication of Peter Simon Pallas' Zoographia Russo-Asiatica includes details of the birds encountered in his journeys through Siberia

events.title: Senjawin
events.text: Russian Senjawin expedition. Heinrich von Kittlitz collects 754 specimens of 314 bird species, including unique specimens of species that subsequently became extinct to the museum of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

events.title: The Birds of Australia
events.text: John Gould publishes the first part of The Birds of Australia

events.title: Alfred Newton
events.text: Alfred Newton forms the British Ornithologists' Union

events.title: Christoph Gottfried Andreas Giebel
events.text: Christoph Gottfried Andreas Giebel begins Thesaurus ornithologiae

events.title: Bombay Natural History Society
events.text: Foundation of the Bombay Natural History Society

events.title: Giovanni Batista Grassi
events.text: Giovanni Batista Grassi and Raimondo Feletti discover avian malaria

events.title: National Audubon Society
events.text: Foundation of the National Audubon Society

events.title: barn swallow
events.text: A barn swallow ringed by James Masefield in Staffordshire, England is recovered in Natal, South Africa

events.title: Perrine Millais Moncrieff
events.text: Perrine Millais Moncrieff publishes a field guide New Zealand Birds and How to Identify Them.

events.title: Brian Roberts
events.text: Brian Roberts is the expedition ornithologist on John Rymill's British Graham Land Expedition (BGLE).

events.title: Rocket nets developed by the Wildfowl Trust for catching geese
events.text: Rocket nets developed by the Wildfowl Trust for catching geese

events.title: G. Evelyn Hutchinson
events.text: G. Evelyn Hutchinson develops the niche concept

events.title: First national breeding bird atlas project conducted in Britain and Ir
events.text: First national breeding bird atlas project conducted in Britain and Ireland

events.title: The Birds of the Western Palearctic
events.text: Publication of the first volume of The Birds of the Western Palearctic

references.label: The Birds of the Western Palearctic

events.title: Bird Studies Canada
events.text: Avibase database commenced by Bird Studies Canada. At 2010 the database holds 5 million records of 10,000 species (22,000 subspecies) and has online World checklists, taxonomic notes and multilingual synonyms.

events.title: host-specific
events.text: Harold Lisle Gibbs, Michael D. Sorenson, Karen Marchetti, Nick Davies, M. de L. Brooke and Hiroshi Nakamura provide genetic evidence for female host-specific races of the common cuckoo

events.title: Neoaves
events.text: A genomic study updated Neoaves and proposed the clade Elementaves.
